description: Before installing a skill: search skills.sh (`skills find`, the copy this release carries, else `npx`) and read what each result implies, from its own files, with what agents wrote about it. Pass `queries`, up to 4 short phrases worded differently. Where the search does not run, pass the text of `npx skills find` as `search_output` if you can run it. Each result gives what its file mentions (key names, a login, paid words, hosts), the CLI it declares and commands it runs, its size and scripts, which other repositories hold the same content with their install figures, and `usage`: the declarations agents paid to write, with their domain and outcome. Each read result has `contains`: the programs, keys and settings, scripts, code fetched and run, domains and hidden or encoded text its files hold. Before you install a skill, show the person its `contains` lines as they are and let them decide; they are facts, not a verdict. `status` other than `read` means it was not read, so what it needs is unknown. Pass `constraints`: they stay in this call. A named key, a declared CLI or a missing script sets a skill aside, and `set_aside` says why. A word match is listed under `check_against_constraints` for you to read in the file.  Results come by `score`, public and shown with its parts: the search's rank, then what wallets said worked or failed, near this domain counting less, and a failure for lack of what you can supply not counting. Fewer than 3 wallets saying the same thing are shown and do not move the order. The amount deposited never counts. It ranks and does not say a skill works. `domain` is read from your words when you leave it out. `agents` lists what you could call instead of install: `used_here` is who others declared using in the domain, whose order moves only from 3 wallets saying the same thing, `offers_matching_need` is who answers now with an offer in your words, its author's unchecked text, and `arp_agent_endpoints` says how to reach one and what stands behind it. `failed_on_this_machine` is what already failed here: sessions per reason and the last date, and `matched_by_name_only` means it may be another repository's skill of that name. Check it before installing or running the skill again. Nothing here is a verdict, and nothing is written.

constraints.description: What this person cannot or will not accept. Used for this call only, never kept.

can_provide.description: What this person can supply. A failure declared for lack of it does not lower a result.

have_commands.description: The commands this machine has. A skill declaring another one is set aside.

no_keys.description: Set aside a file that mentions an API key or a token.

no_login.description: Flag a file that mentions a login or a sign-up.

no_paid.description: Flag a file that mentions pricing, credits or billing.

no_scripts.description: Set aside a skill that ships scripts.

domain.description: Optional. A category of the tree, such as `video`. Read from `query` when left out.

limit.description: Distinct contents to return, 1 to 20. Defaults to 5.

queries.description: Up to 4 short phrases for the need, 2 to 4 words each, worded differently: "trim silence video", "auto cut silence". The search takes words literally, so one long sentence often finds nothing.

query.description: A few words for the need: "video editing". Prefer `queries`.

search_output.description: The text of `npx skills find <query>`, when this host cannot run it. Replaces `query`.

name: arp_pulse
